newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: Trinidad prime minister Panday sets off for India.
newsitem.headline: Trinidad prime minister Panday sets off for India.

text.p: Prime Minister Basdeo Panday set off late on Monday for India where he will pay an official 14-day visit, a government statement said.
He was invited by Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma and will attend India's Republic Day celebrations on Jan. 26.
Panday was accompanied by the ministers of Foreign Affairs, Ralph Maraj, and Trade and Industry, Mervyn Assam, and a large delegation of local business leaders.
The 64-year-old lawyer and trade unionist who heads a coalition government was sworn in as Trinidad and Tobago's first Indian prime minister on Nov. 9, 1995.
Panday is the grandson of indentured labourers brought to work on British-owned sugar plantations in Trinidad in 1908.
